messages:
kevin: hey, trying to /deploy prod release/feature-x and deploy-bot returns permission denied. I'm listed in prod-deployers — anyone seen this?

deploy-bot: Permission check failed for user kevin: not in allowed group for this change window. Allowed groups: eng-release-leads, oncall-deployers. See https://redwood.link/prod-deploy-access. To request temporary access run: `/request-temp-access @kevin --reason <reason>`

anna: hmm, we rotated the prod-deployers list last month. Are you in the monthly rotation this cycle?

kevin: checked the group in Okta — I am. Okta shows MFA_ok = false for my session though. I restarted SSO and re-authed, still the same error.

sara: ops FYI we tightened the change-window policy this week: outside of scheduled windows only oncall-deployers can run prod deploys. During our 22:00-00:00 UTC release window eng-release-leads + oncall-deployers can. Otherwise temp elevation required.

devon: to add: we also started automatic whitelist rotation every 30 days. If you were added >30d ago, you might be on the previous cycle and need re-approval.

kevin: ah that would explain it. How do I get re-approved quickly? This is a hotfix; need to push now.

liz: short path: file a temp-access request in #eng-oncall (use the template) and ping me. Put justification + ticket link. I can approve emergency 2-hour elevation if it's a real prod-blocker and an SRE signs off.

kevin: filed ticket: https://redwood.issues/INC-8421 — hotfix for model-serving timeout regression. tagged @liz @tom.

tom: @liz I reviewed logs, agree it's a production blocker. If you approve, ops-bot can grant `/grant-temp-access` which creates an audit entry and expires automatically.

liz: approving now. Command: `/grant-temp-access @kevin --reason "hotfix INC-8421" --expires 2h`

ops-bot: Temporary access granted: user=kevin, scope=prod-deploy, expires=1782514276 (2h). Approved_by=liz. Audit: grant-id=gr-20260315-33.

deploy-bot: run check: permission OK for user kevin. You can proceed with `/deploy prod release/feature-x --strategy canary`

kevin: running now: `/deploy prod release/feature-x --strategy canary --note "hotfix INC-8421"`

deploy-bot: Deploy started: release/feature-x -> prod (canary). ID=dep-9876. Notifying oncall. Logs: `task=deploy status=started user=kevin`

kevin: can confirm canary healthy after 10m. No errors in logs. proceeding to full rollout.

deploy-bot: Deploy finished: success. ID=dep-9876. Duration=14m. Artifacts: s3://redwood-deploys/prod/dep-9876.

kevin: thanks everyone. Note for postmortem: update the rotation calendar so folks know to reapply if they fall out of the 30d window.

anna: agreed — I'll add a short section to the release runbook and ping infra to email the active list before each rotation.

liz: small follow-ups: 1) if you're granted temp access, assume it expires exactly at the TTL — no exceptions. 2) any emergency elevation must be logged with a follow-up blameless post describing why it was needed.

kevin: ack. leaving notes in INC-8421 and closing after regression monitor. :tada:
